knowledge_passages.content:
### [w1-erosion:baseline]
Leading-edge erosion initiates when rain, hail, or particulates impact the protective coating at tip speeds exceeding 80 m/s. Early-stage wear appears as matte streaking and minor pitting concentrated between 20–40% span, often without exposed fibers.

### [w2-progression:interval_model]
Progression models calibrated on North Sea fleets show a median 0.35 probability that S2 erosion escalates to S3 within 90 days when left untreated, assuming average precipitation and no icing. The risk increases to 0.55 by 180 days absent mitigation.

### [w3-environment:freeze_thaw]
Cold-weather regimes with frequent freeze-thaw cycles cause moisture ingress to expand micro-cracks. When combined with existing erosion, this mechanism can double the likelihood of laminate exposure within 180 days.

### [w4-shm:sensor_array]
Fiber Bragg grating sensors positioned near the blade root detect strain anomalies associated with crack initiation. Deviations greater than 150 microstrain from baseline trigger follow-up NDT within 14 days.

### [w4-shm:scada_correlation]
Coupling SHM data with SCADA power curves improves detection sensitivity by 30%. When both systems flag anomalies, the posterior probability of a true S2 crack exceeds 0.6.

### [w8-logistics:weather_windows]
Offshore repair scheduling depends on weather windows with significant wave height below 1.5 m and wind speeds under 12 m/s. Average waiting time in winter exceeds 18 days, extending risk exposure.
